subject: Delphic Silo — on-prem cluster provisioning, rack-slicing & retention matrix
messages:
From: Daniel Ortiz <daniel.ortiz@fieldfoundry.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: ops+eng@fieldfoundry.com
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Delphic site intake — inventory attached, a few architectural questions

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for taking this. I attached a quick CSV with rack-level inventory and a PNG sketch of the proposed network (nothing final). High-level asks from our infra team:

- We need guidance on whether to present NVMe-oF or local NVMe as the primary PV class for LLM shards. The site has 2x ToR switches per rack (dual-fabric) and a small 25Gb spine.
- Retention: some models (audit logs + KV cache snapshots) must be kept on-site for 90 days, others can be replicated to our central S3 archive daily.
- We have an existing SAN for legacy workloads (iSCSI), but prefer to avoid SAN for inference if possible.

Can Redwood outline a suggested storage tiering + PV class approach and any node sizing recommendations? Also, do you need us to separate racks into "sensitive" vs "shared" tenant zones before the preflight?

Attachments: delphic-site-inventory.csv (CSV, 45KB), network-topology-sketch.png (PNG, 120KB)

Thanks,
Daniel Ortiz
Engineering Manager, FieldFoundry

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Ortiz <daniel.ortiz@fieldfoundry.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Delphic site intake — inventory attached, a few architectural questions

Hi Daniel — thanks for the inventory. Quick responses and next steps below. I copied Karthik and Laura to capture node and storage specifics.

Summary guidance (short):
- Prefer local NVMe (host-attached) for hot LLM shards that need sub-10ms tail latency. Use NVMe-oF for mid-tier models if you must consolidate across racks, but that increases operational complexity and requires consistent RDMA fabric (which your 25Gb spine may not deliver reliably).
- Keep: audit logs + KV snapshots on an on-site encrypted blockstore with daily replication to central S3. We'll propose a two-tier PV strategy: "hot-nvme (local)" + "archive-block (replicated, encrypted)."
- Tenant zoning: yes — mark 1 rack (or 2 small racks) as "sensitive" for regulated model footprints; enforce nodeSelectors + topologySpread (zone=fault-domain) so workloads never span same ToR for redundancy.

Deliverables we will produce for preflight:
1) Node sizing matrix (CPU/GPUs/RAM/NVMe capacity) tailored to your model mix.
2) PV class recommendation and CSI driver setup steps (including encryption-at-rest details).
3) A short runbook for cutover: pre-provisioning, canary pods, and emergency rollback.

Questions for you (please reply inline if possible):
- Can you confirm the intended model mix (token throughput expectation) for production? Even a weekly 95th percentile token estimate helps.
- Is the SAN administratively isolated from the proposed inference racks? (We need to know SAN availability for fallback.)
- Any regulatory constraints on key management? Do you require a customer-managed KMS/HSM?

I'll draft the Node sizing matrix and PV mapping; Karthik will validate the networking and Laura will add the storage QoS knobs. Target: initial proposal by Friday EOD (2027-07-02).

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Sr. Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Fw: Delphic site intake — notes on fabric and ToR

Priya / Laura — forwarding my raw network notes after a call with FieldFoundry's network lead. Paste of our internal notes below for the proposal.

--- Forwarded message ---
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 10:30:00 -07:00
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Subject: internal: fabric notes (for Delphic)

- The dual ToR setup is fine if we treat each ToR as a separate fault domain. PodTopologySpread should be configured to prefer distinct fault domains.
- 25Gb spine -> NVMe-oF will be flaky under peak (RDMA/ROCE needs 100Gb or careful QoS). Recommend: use host-local NVMe for hot, and plan a mid-term upgrade path for 100Gb fabric if they want NVMe-oF across racks.
- For blockstore fallback: mount iSCSI as emergency read-only PV (not for active KV cache).
- BGP egress: confirm whether customer wants control plane egress through primary site NAT or through a separate egress appliance. That affects our image pull proxy planning.

I'll annotate the node-sizing with expected network egress (MB/s per shard). Karthik

From: Daniel Ortiz <daniel.ortiz@fieldfoundry.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: ops+eng@fieldfoundry.com
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2027 16:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Delphic site intake — inventory attached, a few architectural questions

Thanks — this is exactly the kind of direction we wanted. Attached is an updated CSV with token-throughput estimates and a revised topology (see provisioning-MAP_v2.docx). High level answers:

- Model mix: two production TGI-style models (one ~350 tps 95th estimate, one ~120 tps) plus a handful of smaller fine-tuned adapters.
- SAN is administratively separate but reachable; we'd prefer read-only fallback only.
- Key management: customer-managed KMS required (we use Vault + HSM in HQ).
- Egress: route control-plane egress through primary NAT, but we'd like a mirror appliance for large image pulls during provisioning windows.

Next step for us: confirm the Node sizing matrix and PV class names so we can prep rack labelling and KMS access prior to the on-site window (target week of 2027-07-18).

Attachments: provisioning-MAP_v2.docx (DOCX, 85KB)

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

—Daniel
Engineering Manager, FieldFoundry
